LESSON: READING 1.2.1EXTENSIVE READING: INDEPENDENT READING

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.2: Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading, part of Strand 1 in Grade 8 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why should one read widely? 2. What should one consider when selecting a reading text?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. skim through grade-appropriate print and electronic reading materials,

2. scan grade-appropriate print and electronic reading materials,

3. read materials on human rights at their pace within a specified period,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. skim through grade-appropriate print and electronic reading materials,
2. scan grade-appropriate print and electronic reading materials,
3. read materials on human rights at their pace within a specified period,

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Self–efficacy: This is enhanced when the learner improves their self-esteem as they choose the texts to read.

• Learning to learn: It is enhanced as the learner gains assertiveness and independence when they select reading materials.

Values:
Responsibility: It is developed as the learner engages and helps peers in selecting reading materials.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Decision-making: This is improved as the learner chooses what to read extensively from a variety of materials.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner relates the concept of human rights to the study of other learning areas such as Social Studies which handles

human rights as a pertinent issue.
